# Appeal of Denial — Total Shoulder Replacement (CPT 23472)

**Date:** [Date this letter is mailed]

**To:** Humana — Grievances and Appeals
[Grievances and Appeals PO Box address printed on my denial letter]

**From:**
Quinn Carter
Member ID: W589686059
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

---

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 11, 2026**
**Member:** Quinn Carter — **Member ID:** W589686059
**Reference number:** POC-3B4A598A17-15463
**Service denied:** Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
**Plan:** Humana (Commercial/ACA), State of Arizona

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing Humana's denial of the prior authorization request for a total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472). The denial notice is dated August 11, 2026 and carries reference number POC-3B4A598A17-15463. I am asking Humana to reconsider that decision and to approve this surgery, which my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented is medically necessary for me.

## A note on the plan's criteria

Humana's notice states that the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity, and refers generally to the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. However, no criteria were quoted to me, and no specific medical policy, section, or threshold was identified in the notice or provided with it. **For that reason, I am not quoting any plan language in this letter — I have not been given any to quote.** Everything below is drawn from my own medical records.

I am asking Humana, in writing and as part of this appeal, to provide me with:

1. The complete text of the specific medical policy and clinical review criteria that were applied to my request;
2. The particular criterion or criteria my records were found not to meet, and the reason;
3. The name and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination.

Humana is the party that holds these criteria and applied them. I cannot meaningfully respond to a standard I have not been shown, and I would ask that this appeal be held open so that I may supplement it once the criteria are provided.

## What my records show

My surgeon's prior authorization packet documents the following. I have listed the findings exactly as my records state them:

**Length and course of symptoms.** I have had 14 months of progressive pain in the shoulder, and it is not relieved by rest.

**Conservative treatment, completed and documented.**
- **Physical therapy:** supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening — 12 weeks, from March 28, 2026 to June 20, 2026, with 24 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** NSAIDs for 6 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** a corticosteroid injection on April 6, 2026, which gave 4 weeks of partial relief.

**Imaging.** Shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary) taken June 12, 2026 show complete loss of glenohumeral joint space, with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. CT confirms an intact rotator cuff.

**Physical examination.** Glenohumeral crepitus; active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees; external rotation limited to 10 degrees; cuff strength intact.

**Effect on my daily life.** I cannot reach overhead. I cannot dress without help. I cannot sleep on the affected side.

**Surgical safety factors.** I have no active infection and no untreated substance use. My BMI is 29. I am a non-smoker.

This is a record of joint disease that is visible on imaging as complete loss of joint space, confirmed on examination, and unrelieved after more than a year of symptoms and a full course of non-surgical treatment — therapy, medication, and injection — each of which was tried and documented before surgery was requested. My surgeon has documented that the procedure is needed.

If Humana's criteria include requirements regarding symptom duration, the amount or length of conservative care, imaging findings, range of motion, or functional limitation, I would ask the reviewer to compare each of those requirements directly against the findings listed above. I am not in a position to state what those requirements are, because they have not been shared with me.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask Humana to:

1. Overturn the denial dated August 11, 2026 and authorize CPT 23472;
2. Provide me the written criteria and reviewer information described above; and
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician board-certified in orthopedic surgery.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **February 7, 2027**. I am obtaining the appeal form at **resolutions.humana.com** (online form: resolutions.humana.com/grievances-appeals-forms) and mailing it to the Grievances and Appeals PO Box. For an expedited request, the address is P.O. Box 14165, and the expedited phone line is **1-800-867-6601**, or the number on my member card. I am using the appeal address and deadline printed on my denial letter, which is the authoritative source for both.

Enclosed with this letter are: [list enclosures — e.g., copy of the denial notice, physical therapy discharge note dated 2026-06-20, imaging report dated 2026-06-12, office notes from Dr. Lindqvist, medication and injection records].

Thank you for reviewing this appeal. I can be reached at [my phone number] or [my email address] if anything further is needed.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Quinn Carter**
